re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:07:41Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 80

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 885

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

---

### Thread 7 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` line 200

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch
re-creates all three as `io`/`cleanEnv`/`cleanRoot` with identical expressions.
Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a
`--cwd` handling the other forgets). Same for the `FileSessionPresenceStore`
wiring, which is copied verbatim from the repair branch.

---

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.
"}

Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified

  Actual: ['sessions']

must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in

```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.
"}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:07:41Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart

'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.
"}

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart

'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private

same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.
"}

// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty

Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:07:41Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart

'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private

same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

Two related nits in the walk:

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").

   knowable from args but never passed).

   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:07:41Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 80

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private

same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 885

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the

least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart

'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private

same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.
